PP2 · Chapter 3 of 7

Flat shapes and solid things

Connect shapes to real objects and simple position clues.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Add and take away. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can count sides and corners.
  • I can recognise a solid by how it moves.
  • I can join shapes to make a picture.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Count sides and corners

A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.

A square and a rectangle have 4.

A circle has no sides and no corners.

Screen 2 of 4

Solid things

Solids are shapes you can hold.

A ball is a sphere. A box is a cube or a cuboid.

A tin is a cylinder.

Screen 3 of 4

Rolls or slides?

A sphere rolls and rolls.

A cube has flat faces. It slides, it does not roll.

Screen 4 of 4

Shapes make a picture

A square, a triangle, a rectangle and a circle.

Put them together and they make a house.

Words to know
side
A straight edge of a flat shape.
corner
A pointy place where two sides meet.
solid
A shape you can hold, like a ball or a box.
roll
To turn over and over, like a ball.

For parents

What your child learns

Your child counts the sides and corners of flat shapes, names solids by how they move, and builds pictures from shapes.

A common slip

Mixing up a flat shape with a solid, like circle and sphere. A circle is flat. A sphere is a ball you can hold.

5-minute home activity: Roll or slide

  1. Find a ball, a tin, a box and a dice.
  2. Ask your child to guess which will roll.
  3. Push each one gently across the floor.
  4. Name each solid together.
